2026-12-15.weatherAlert: Typical December evenings in Tokyo are cold and dry, but an occasional rain shower is possible. The Kabukicho neon walk and Omoide Yokocho are mostly exposed.
tips: Hit the Limousine Bus ATM or convenience store to break large bills; small yakiniku stalls under the tracks are cash-only.
If wide awake at 4am JST, embrace the jet lag: walk to the Tokyo Metropolitan Gov't Building for a free sunrise view or hit a 24h gyudon counter.

2026-12-16.weatherAlert: Rain risk for the outdoor Shibuya Blue Cave illumination walk and Meiji Shrine forest walk. December can bring sudden cold rain.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Shibuya Blue Cave illumination — ~600k blue LEDs toward Yoyogi
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: Miyashita Park covered rooftop + Parco + Tower Records (9 floors) absorb a full wet afternoon without surfacing.
suggestedSwap.reason: The Blue Cave illumination is an outdoor walk along Yoyogi Park that loses its magic in heavy December rain; Miyashita Park and Parco offer covered, indoor alternatives right in Shibuya.

tips: Shibuya Sky sunset slots sell out fast; if you haven't pre-booked, try the free Shibuya Hikarie 11F Sky Lobby for great crossing views.
Nomihodai (all-you-can-drink) izakayas require everyone in the group to participate—decide as a squad before sitting down.

2026-12-17.weatherAlert: Outdoor market day at Nakamise and Ameyoko; cold, wet December conditions can make uncovered market streets slippery and miserable.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Ueno Ameyoko market under the tracks
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: Tokyo National Museum (samurai swords + armor, 2h) slots between Asakusa and Akiba on the same line.
suggestedSwap.reason: Ameyoko is an open-air market that is unpleasant in heavy rain; the Tokyo National Museum is a short walk away in Ueno Park and offers world-class indoor warmth.

tips: Skytree night slots often have long lines. If the queue is insane, head next door to the Asahi Beer Hall's 22F Sky Room for the same river view with a beer.
Kamiya Bar in Asakusa (est. 1880) serves the famous Denki Bran 'electric brandy' for about ¥350—a perfect pre-Skytree warm-up.
teamLab Planets requires stepping into water; they provide rental towels, but wear easy-slip shoes and roll-up pants.
Golden Gai bars seat 5-6 people max; split into smaller squads and hop between alleys to maximize the experience.

2026-12-19.weatherAlert: High rain risk for this coastal day trip. The Enoshima island climb and Fuji-over-Sagami-Bay sunset view are heavily weather-dependent.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Enoshima island — climb to the Sea Candle
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Enoshima onsen finish: Enospa overlooks the bay — soak with a Fuji view before the train if legs are cooked.
suggestedSwap.reason: If it's raining, climbing Enoshima's outdoor stairs to the Sea Candle is miserable, but Enospa provides a warm, indoor onsen with bay views regardless of the weather.

tips: The Enoden coastal tram is scenic but slow; if connecting from Hase-dera, check the timetable to avoid a long wait in the cold.
December offers peak Mt. Fuji clarity, but only from a distance. If it's overcast in Kamakura, cut losses and head back to Shinjuku early for a cozy gyukatsu dinner.
Ghibli Museum tickets are strictly timed and non-refundable; arrive 10 minutes early or risk being denied entry.
Run the Airbnb laundry during dinner so everyone lands in Kyoto with a clean kit—logistics IS culture.

2026-12-21.weatherAlert: Gion's golden hour and the Kamo River bank hangout are outdoor evening activities vulnerable to cold December rain.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Kamo River bank — konbini cans, December stars
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: Kyoto International Manga Museum — 50,000 manga, huge English wall, a school where you just sit and read. Dangerous time vortex.
suggestedSwap.reason: Sitting on the Kamo River bank in cold December rain holds zero appeal; the Manga Museum offers a massive, dry, indoor sanctuary for the group to relax.

tips: Grab ekiben (train bento) at Tokyo Station's Ekibenya Matsuri before boarding—there are 200+ kinds and it's part of the Shinkansen experience.
For the left-side Fuji view on the Nozomi, reserve seats A, B, or C; minute 40 is the sweet spot.

2026-12-22.weatherAlert: Fushimi Inari at dawn involves a long outdoor ascent; December mornings are freezing, and rain makes the stone paths extremely slippery.
tips: Layer up for Fushimi Inari—it's colder on the mountain than in the city. Vending machine hot corn soup on the descent is a lifesaver.
Funaoka Onsen has tattoo-friendly hours; check the schedule if anyone in the group has ink to avoid a last-minute denial.

2026-12-23.weatherAlert: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove before the buses is an outdoor, exposed walkway. December rain makes the bamboo dark and the paths slick.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Iwatayama Monkey Park — humans enter the cage
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Kimono Forest at Randen Arashiyama station: pillar-lit fabric columns glowing at dusk — free, on the way out anyway.
suggestedSwap.reason: The hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park is steep and becomes dangerous in December rain; the Kimono Forest is right at the station, covered, and beautiful in any weather.

tips: Wakakusa-yama is closed for the winter (since Dec 13); do not attempt the climb today.
When feeding Nara's deer, bow first, show empty hands when done, and never run—they read it as a game they will win.

2026-12-24.weatherAlert: Dotonbori and Hozenji Yokocho are mostly covered, but the walk between them and the Ebisubashi bridge people-watching are exposed to cold rain.
tips: Pre-order your KFC Christmas Bucket! This is a sacred Japanese tradition and buckets sell out fast—check the app or local store days in advance.
If you missed the Nintendo Museum lottery, Uji still delivers: Byodo-in, Tsuen tea, and matcha soba make for a perfect rainy morning.

2026-12-25.crowdAlert: USJ on Christmas Day will be at peak capacity. Super Nintendo World timed entry and Express Passes are absolute necessities.
tips: Rope-drop the park 45 minutes early and head straight to Super Nintendo World; wait times exceed 2 hours by 10am.
If the group splits, non-USJ folks can hit Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan (also crowded, but manageable) and the nearby Tempozan wheel.

2026-12-26.weatherAlert: Miyajima's floating torii and the Omotesando street oyster crawl are entirely outdoors and exposed to Inland Sea winds and rain.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Omotesando street — GRILLED OYSTERS + fried momiji manju
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Oyster maximalists: kakigoya grill-huts operate near the Miyajima pier in season. $13 (¥2,000) of shells, zero regrets.
suggestedSwap.reason: If heavy rain hits, walking the long Omotesando shopping street is a soggy affair; the covered kakigoya grill-huts near the pier offer a warm, sheltered oyster alternative.

tips: This is the longest day of the trip. Anyone redlining should skip Miyajima, do the Peace Museum unhurried, and meet at Hiroshima station.
The Peace Memorial Museum is emotionally heavy; Shukkei-en garden is a 10-minute walk away and offers a quiet, beautiful space to decompress.

2026-12-27.weatherAlert: The Midosuji Illumination walk is a 4km outdoor boulevard; cold December rain can wash out the experience.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: MIDOSUJI ILLUMINATION — 4km of lit boulevard, walked south
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Osaka Museum of Housing & Living: walk a life-size Edo street in a rented yukata — sleeper-hit rain plan, 15 min north.
suggestedSwap.reason: Walking 4km in cold December rain is miserable; the Osaka Museum of Housing & Living offers an incredible, fully indoor, life-size Edo street experience nearby.

tips: Buy a 551 Horai butaman 4-pack from Namba station BEFORE the crab dinner—they sell out nightly and house breakfast depends on it.
Tax-free paperwork check tonight: ensure receipts are with passports and purchases are accessible—customs CAN ask on exit.

2026-12-28.weatherAlert: Himeji Castle involves extensive outdoor walking and steep climbs; December rain makes the white plaster slippery and the wind off the plains biting.
tips: Kobe beef lunch is a splurge; if the budget is sweating, the ¥3,500 Kobe-beef bowls and croquette stands around Sannomiya deliver 70% of the experience at 40% of the price.
Nada sake district (Hakutsuru brewery museum, free with tastings) is two stops from Sannomiya—a perfect Gekkeikan rematch before heading home.
For the final Shinkansen sprint, sit on the LEFT (seats A) for Mt. Fuji's encore around minute 40.
Zero out your Suica card today: use it for final konbini runs or airside meals, as foreign cards cannot be refunded easily.

globalTips: With the USD/JPY rate at ~161.65, your dollar stretches far. Avoid exchanging cash at airport kiosks with high fees; withdraw directly from 7-Eleven ATMs for the best rates.

December in Japan is cold and dry, but rain is always possible. Pack a compact, lightweight rain jacket and comfortable, water-resistant walking shoes—umbrellas are a hassle on crowded trains and in shrines.
For a group of 8, always split into smaller squads of 2-4 for restaurants, bars, and peak sightseeing—Japanese venues rarely seat 8 together, and you'll navigate crowds much faster.
